correctness.rationale: For every external cell (i,j), its number of white neighbors in the rook graph is r_i+c_j. Thus W is a fort iff no external cell has r_i+c_j=1. Classifying whether there are empty rows/columns forces: full row/column transversals for the exceptional 2×2, 2×3 and 3×3 cases; 2×2 rectangles when both sides admit an empty row/column; and 2-whites-in-each-row families when m=2. The n=4 four-cell full-column configurations contribute exactly 8,36,24 exceptional configurations for 2×4, 3×4, 4×4. Choosing 2 rows/columns counts binom(m,2)binom(n,2) rectangles; the thin board has binom(n,2)^2 independent row-pair choices. A maximal-cardinality failed blue set must be stalled, because forcing one more vertex would yield a larger still-failed set; complements of stalled sets are exactly forts. An independent adjacency-defined finite enumerator reproduced the classification on 2≤m≤5,m≤n≤6. No finite test was substituted for the all-m,n proof.
